column1: # The tools ONLY THIS REPO'S OWN steps need, one per line.
# THE RULE: every non-comment line must be a step in `.gatesrc`'s `GOH_CI_STEPS`.
# A name is here because a step in that list runs it, and nothing else may put one
# here -- a tool no step needs is one the runner installs for nothing, which is
# the same drift in the opposite direction. `tools/tests/test_ci_tools.py` goes
# red, naming the line, when a name here stops being a step there.
# WHY THIS IS SEPARATE FROM THE GATE'S MANIFEST. `"$GOH_DIR/gates/required_tools.py"
# --repo . --install` names the tools its own gates REFUSE without -- measured
# 2026-10-08: cargo-machete, cargo-llvm-cov, ruff, shellcheck; since goh 0.27.0's
# advisory step, cargo-audit as well, so it left this file (a tool both lists name
# is installed twice, and `cargo install` refuses the second:
# tools/tests/test_ci_tools.py goes red on the overlap). It cannot name
# cargo-deny, because `cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml check` is a step
# THIS repo added to GOH_CI_STEPS (2026-10-05: licences, sources and bans). A shared
# manifest has no way to know a consumer grew a step, which is exactly how the
# hand-copied list rotted: run 37855122727 died at step 1/12 with
# `cargo-machete is not installed, and this gate does not pass without the step it
# runs`. So the workflow consumes the manifest for its half and reads this file
# for the rest, and neither half is copied by hand.
# HOW IT IS READ: ci.yml's install step strips `#` comments, drops the lines left
# empty, and joins what is left with commas for taiki-e/install-action's `tool:`
# input. A line that survives that read is a tool the runner will install.
# NOT a .txt. `.gitignore:149` ignores `*.txt` (only `tests/fixtures/**/*.txt` is
# excepted), so this file as a .txt would be untrackable -- invisible to the gate
# AND to CI, which read it and installed nothing while the step passed.
cargo-deny
